summary: Verified FRONTEND_URL fix for POST /api/auth/forgot-password. All 4 backend pytest cases pass: (1) reset link starts with https://roadtrip-tracker-2.preview.emergentagent.com and never contains cluster-3.preview.emergentcf.cloud; (2) spoofed Origin/Referer headers (evil.example.com) are ignored — link still built from FRONTEND_URL env; (3) GET on the reset link returns HTTP 200, no 403; (4) full E2E: forgot-password -> parse link -> reset-password -> login with new password -> reset back to admin123 -> login with admin123 all succeed. Admin credentials restored to admin@roadtrip.com / admin123.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1102 lines — consider splitting into modules (auth, events, users) for maintainability.

forgot_password returns reset_link in response body when Resend delivery.sent is False — safe for dev but should be gated behind an explicit env flag (e.g. DEBUG_RETURN_RESET_LINK) so production can never accidentally leak tokens if Resend has an outage.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reset flow now uses FRONTEND_URL env var (backend/.env). If FRONTEND_URL is unset, code falls back to Origin/Referer header which yields the broken internal cluster URL — keep FRONTEND_URL set. Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_forgot_password.py can be reused; requires REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL env var when running pytest.
rca of the issue: Original bug: reset_link built from request Origin header, which Kubernetes ingress rewrote to internal cluster host (cluster-3.preview.emergentcf.cloud) that returns 403 to external users. Fix: read FRONTEND_URL from backend/.env (https://roadtrip-tracker-2.preview.emergentagent.com) and prefer it over Origin/Referer. Verified working end-to-end.
